question: Build a primary-source panel of DAF clauses in the matching-gift guidelines of the largest US corporate programmes (Fortune 100 plus the top corporate foundations by matching spend), dated 2021 or later. Use public company PDFs and portal terms only. Classify each clause: grants from DAFs accepted / conditional (sole funder, named on fund) / excluded / silent; gifts into DAFs excluded
conclusion_affected: Whether matching-gift eligibility is a feature a DAF entrant must build (grant confirmations, donor certification) and how much DAF grant volume is match-eligible
rationale: Of 16 policies found, only GE (2023), Disney (2021) and EY (2022) are dated 2021+ primary documents. The rest are 2025 secondary quotes or pre-2021 PDFs. The common pattern is conditional acceptance: the DAF must be funded solely by the employee, or the employee must be named on it; gifts into DAFs are excluded. Bank of America's quoted text is ambiguous and Dow's is contradictory
